Frequently.title: How much does it cost to build a healthcare app?
Frequently.desc: The healthcare app development cost depends on the app’s complexity, features, and platform (iOS, Android, or both). On average, a basic healthcare app may cost between $25,000 to $80,000, while advanced apps with telemedicine, AI, or IoT integrations can range from $100,000 to $250,000. Comfygen offers affordable and scalable healthcare app development services tailored to your business goals.

Frequently.title: How long does it take to develop a healthcare app?
Frequently.desc: The medical mobile application development timeline varies depending on the project scope. A simple app may take 2–3 months, while feature-rich healthcare solutions with integrations and compliance testing can take 4–8 months. At Comfygen Technologies, we follow an Agile development approach to deliver faster results without compromising quality or compliance.

Frequently.title: How does Comfygen ensure compliance in medical app development?
Frequently.desc: We strictly follow global healthcare standards such as HIPAA, GDPR, and HL7 to ensure your medical app meets all regulatory and data privacy requirements. Our team implements advanced encryption protocols, secure authentication, and data access control measures to guarantee complete patient data protection.

Frequently.title: Can you integrate telemedicine features?
Frequently.desc: Yes, absolutely! Our expert healthcare app developers can integrate advanced telemedicine features such as secure video consultations, real-time chat, e-prescriptions, and digital health records. Frequently.desc: Yes, we specialize in AI-powered healthcare app development. Our team can implement AI-driven chatbots, predictive analytics, diagnostic tools, patient behavior insights, and virtual health assistants to enhance care delivery, automation, and patient engagement within your app.

myList: HIPAA (Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act): Ensures the privacy and security of patients' health information in the U.S.
GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation): Applies to companies dealing with personal data in the EU, ensuring data protection and privacy.
FDA (Food and Drug Administration) Regulations: Required for software classified as medical devices in the U.S., ensuring safety and efficacy.
HITECH (Health Information Technology for Economic and Clinical Health Act): Works in conjunction with HIPAA to promote the adoption of health information technology while ensuring data security.
ISO 13485: Specifies requirements for quality management systems used by organizations that develop medical devices and healthcare software.
CFR Title 21 Part 11: U.S. FDA regulation for electronic records and signatures, applicable to healthcare software dealing with sensitive data.
PIPEDA (Personal Information Protection and Electronic Documents Act): Canadian law governing data privacy and how organizations handle personal information.
ONC HIT Certification: A U.S. certification for healthcare technology ensuring that health IT meets specific government standards.

Compliance.title: HIPAA (Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act)
Compliance.decs: HIPAA is a fundamental guideline that governs the handling of personal health information in the United States. Our experts follow the Health Insurance Portability and Accountability Act (HIPAA) guidelines to ensure better security and privacy of protected health information (PHI), ensuring that medical software collects, processes, and stores data securely.

Compliance.title: HITECH (Health Information Technology for Economic and Clinical Health) Act
Compliance.decs: The HITECH Act works alongside HIPAA to promote the adoption and meaningful use of health information technology. HITECH focuses on the implementation of electronic health records and aims to strengthen the protection of health information. As part of our healthcare app development services, we implement the HITECH electronic health record (EHR) system to support your applications with the latest technology.

Compliance.title: FDA (Food and Drug Administration)
Compliance.decs: We develop healthcare mobile application development services, and solutions, that adhere to the guidelines and standards of the FDA, and are responsible for regulating a wide range of products, including medical devices, drugs, and food. For medical software developers, FDA regulations are essential, particularly when creating apps that are considered medical devices or have a medical purpose.

Compliance.title: GDPR (General Data Protection Regulation)
Compliance.decs: During the development of mHealth App Development, we adhere to GDPR and rules. GDPR is a European Union regulation that governs the collection, processing, and storage of personal data. Medical software designed for EU countries must comply with GDPR to protect user data and privacy, with severe penalties for non-compliance. It ensures for secured messaging and encrypted file transfers.

Compliance.title: HL7 (Health Level Seven):
Compliance.decs: HL7 standards facilitate the exchange of health information between different healthcare systems. The HL7 standards enable seamless interoperability and compatibility between medical software and a variety of healthcare applications, allowing the secure transfer of clinical and administrative data between the two systems.
